narrative:
The model estimated an 80.5% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a high-risk prediction, not a certainty, but it was strong enough for the law school to deny your application because schools use bar-passage risk as a key admissions concern.

The denial was driven mainly by your class standing. Your third-year standing was in the lowest decile, far below the average of about the sixth decile among accepted students, and it was the single strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Your first-year standing was also in the lowest decile, compared with an accepted-student average near the sixth decile, and it was the second strongest factor, also pushing toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 2.80 was below the accepted-student average of 3.23; this was the third most influential factor and it pushed toward passing, but it was not enough to outweigh the concerns about class standing.

To improve a future application, focus on a clear upward academic record: take additional rigorous coursework or a post-baccalaureate program, consider retaking the LSAT, seek admissions advising, and document any circumstances behind earlier grades. Reapply when you can show stronger, more recent evidence of bar-exam readiness.
